name: Bass Iron
description: The tone before the valves turned down, so that the lows drive them 3 dB harder and the highs 3 dB less, and the drive at 68: a bass's low notes get a second and a third harmonic 46 dB under them at -12 dBFS, which is what is heard of them on a small speaker, and the transformer's core adds to the lowest.

name: Console Line
description: The stage as a new one stands: the gain at 0 and the drive at 60, where it gives what it takes. A second harmonic 52 dB under a tone at -12 dBFS and 23 dB under one at full scale, where the top of the wave begins to flatten. Leave it on a track that sounds too clean.

name: Drum Bus Push
description: The drive at 75, some 8 dB into the second valve: the hits of a drum bus are flattened on one side and come out 6 dB lower, and what lies under them is left alone. The second harmonic of a tone at -12 dBFS is 41 dB under it.

name: Iron Only
description: The valves out and the transformer in: nothing above 200 Hz is touched, and a low note is given a third harmonic, 55 dB under a tone of 60 Hz at -12 dBFS and 24 dB under one at full scale. For a kick or a bass that wants weight and no colour above it, at a third of the processing.

name: Mix Bus Sheen
description: The gain at -5 and the drive at 66, a dB under where the stage gives what it takes, with its first valve given less, the tone a touch darker before the valves and brighter after: a mix's peaks stay under the knee, and what is added is a second harmonic 55 dB under a tone at -12 dBFS, 36 under one at full scale, and the core's weight on the lowest notes.

name: Odd Bite
description: The bias turned up, toward the second valve's grid conducting, and the drive at 75: under the knee the second harmonic falls away and the third leads, 46 dB under a tone at -12 dBFS with the second 2 dB under that. A drier, more forward colour, for a synth or a guitar that even harmonics make too sweet.

name: Parallel Smash
description: The gain at +10 and the drive at 80, so that both valve stages clip, mixed in at 40 % beside the drums as they came: the crushed signal fills in between the hits and the hits keep their front. For a drum bus or a room microphone.

name: Vocal Edge
description: The gain at +5, the drive at 70, and the tone brighter into the valves and darker after them: the highs of a voice are driven harder than its body and then put back, so the grit sits on the consonants. Every harmonic of a tone at -12 dBFS up to the fifth is within 10 dB of the second, at 30 to 40 dB under it.

name: Vocal Warmth
description: The bias turned down, toward the second valve shutting, and the drive just under where it stands: the second harmonic of a tone at -12 dBFS comes up from 52 to 36 dB under it and the third stays 12 dB under that. Even harmonics on a voice, which thicken it without an edge.
